rationale: Run the probe the trim child question asks for. The new case drifts the recorded accepted indexes with three reconnection rounds, changes the leader so that the new leader's own recorded value is inflated too, and then calls the public trim(None) on that leader with the call wrapped so a panic is reported instead of aborting the run; the samples report each node's accepted and decided index and the trim's outcome, compacted index, accepted index and decided index. The comparisons require the six-index baseline before the trim, that trim(None) reports no error for a configuration whose six indices have been decided, that the compacted index reaches six, and that the leader's decided index stays covered by its entries afterwards; if the drift reaches the trim bound the error outcome and the unchanged compacted index are the witnesses.

experiment.revision_reason: Adds a drift-then-trim case: three reconnection rounds followed by a leader change, so every node's recorded accepted index is inflated, then a public trim(None) on the new leader with the outcome, compacted index and node states sampled.

scope.description: Eight cases in one execution over three real OmniPaxos instances in one process with MemoryStorage and a deterministic FIFO in-process network; the new case drifts the recorded accepted indexes with three reconnection rounds, changes the leader so that the new leader's own recorded value is inflated too, and then calls the public trim(None) on that leader, wrapping the call so a panic is reported as an event field rather than aborting the run.
assumptions: Entry type Value has Snapshot = NoSnapshot; ClusterConfig { configuration_id: 1, nodes: [1,2,3], flexible_quorum: None } with default ServerConfig (batch_size 1).

Three reconnection rounds of node 1 and node 2 are followed by node 2 taking the lead with try_become_leader(), which in this harness inflates the new leader's own recorded accepted index as witnessed by the staleleader stage.
trim is called with None, which the documentation describes as using the highest trimmable index; the call is wrapped in catch_unwind so a panic becomes a reported outcome.
excluded: Snapshots are not exercised; no entry type with use_snapshots() true is used in this case.
No crate or package test suite is executed; only the generated test file.

experiment.prefix: Same prefix as the lineage (node 3 leads, five entries decided, StopSign decided). The new case then performs three rounds of node1.reconnected(3)+node2.reconnected(3) with the queue drained each time, calls node2.try_become_leader() and drains again, samples all three nodes as DRIFTTRIM_BEFORE, calls node2.trim(None) inside catch_unwind and emits DRIFTTRIM_TRIM with trim_outcome (ok/err/panic), compacted_idx, accepted_idx and decided_idx of the leader, then samples all three nodes as DRIFTTRIM_AFTER.

comparisons.description: Baseline of the drift-then-trim case: before the trim the leader still reports six indices of content.
Baseline: before the trim the followers still report six indices of content.
The documented trim path succeeds for a leader whose configuration has decided six indices: trim(None) reports no error.
The configuration's decided prefix reaches the compacted index: trim(None) compacts up to the six indices every node decided.
After the trim the leader's decided index is still covered by the entries it holds.
